title: A Flexible Chamber for Time-Lapse Live-Cell Imaging with Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
protocol: Build the microscope environmental enclosure.
Mark the locations of the feet of the SRS microscope frame and the motorized stage using a marker pen on the optical table.
Mount two Iris Diaphragms in front of the Galvanometer scanner of the microscope.
Adjust the Iris Diaphragms to make the pump and Stokes laser beams pass through the center.
Remove the microscope frame and the stage from the optical table.
Lay the silicone rubber sheet on the optical table.
Cut the silicone rubber along the marks using a knife, remove small rubber pieces.
Place square MICA ceramic sheets into the same locations as the cutouts in the silicone rubber.
Drill through-holes on the MICA sheets to allow the use of ¼-20 screws for mounting.
Move the microscope frame and the stage back to the optical table.
Carefully align the feet onto the MICA ceramic sheets along the marker lines.
Use ¼-20 screws to mount the frame and the stage on the table.
Realign the SRS optical path.
Adjust Mirror 1 mounts to center the laser beam through the first Iris Diaphragm.
Adjust Mirror 2 mounts to center the laser beam through the second Iris Diaphragm.
Cut polycarbonate sheets to size (31 x 29 x 28 inches).
Drill and tap screw holes on each edge of the polycarbonate sheets.
Cut two large holes with a diameter of 2.6 inches on the right and left sheets for tubing.
Cut a small hole with a diameter of 5 mm on the back sheet to allow laser beams entry.
Seal edges and interfaces of the enclosure box using aluminum foil tape.
Connect the flexible duct hose to the inlet and outlet ports of the enclosure box.
Place the thermal sensor of the heater module in the flexible chamber where cells are cultured and imaged.
Set the targeted temperature at 37 °C.
Mount the machined hollow cylindrical aluminum piece 1 to the nosepiece of the objective using three set screws.
Mount the machined hollow cylindrical aluminum piece 2 to the sample holder using four ¼-20 screws.
Drill a through hole in the center of the sample holder using a 1-7/8 inches hole saw.
Counterbore the hole using a 50 mm hole saw and keep the depth of the through hole ~1 mm.
Fit the sample holder with the aluminum piece 2 onto the motorized stage.
Mount the assembled sample holder onto the motorized stage using screws.
Place the natural rubber film sleeve between the two machined aluminum pieces.
Secure the natural rubber film sleeve at each end using rubber bands.
Connect the compressed CO2 cylinder to the gas mixer module using proper tubing and connectors.
Set the CO2 input pressure at 20-25 psi.
Use a built-in CO2 sensor and controller to regulate and mix 5% CO2 into the airflow.
Guide the mixed air (with 5% CO2) through inline filters to clean up the airflow.
Guide the filtered, humidified air to the presterilized water bottle placed on the hot plate using proper tubing and connectors.
Set the hot plate at 37 °C.
Bubble the airflow in the warm water to increase humidity.
Wipe all parts of the flexible chamber with 70% ethanol, including the nosepiece, the water dipping objective, and the sample holder.
Decontaminate the entire enclosure system using a UV lamp placed in the enclosure for 20 to 30 min.
Culture SKOV3 cells in a 50-mm glass-bottom Petri dish for 12 h under normal physiological conditions in a regular incubator.
Disconnect the machined aluminum piece 2 from the sample holder by removing the screws.
Load the cell culture dish.
Add immersion oil on top of the condenser before placing the cell culture dish.
Remove the cover of the dish.
Immobilize the dish using clamps.
Lower the objective into the cell culture media for coarse focusing.
Attach a 2 mm silicone rubber cushion pad to the bottom of aluminum piece 2.
Enclose the flexible chamber with aluminum piece 2 and mount it to the sample holder using screws.
Set the air supply with 5% CO2 and 19% O2 for normal cell culture, maintaining an airflow rate of 200 cc/min.
Tune the laser wavelength to 805 nm to target the 2854 cm-1 Raman shift.
Use ~15 mW average power of the pump laser for long-term live-cell imaging.
Use ~7.5 mW of the Stokes laser (fixed at 1,045 nm) for long-term live-cell imaging.
Adjust the objective to achieve good SRS imaging of the cells.
Use the FOCUS button on the MAIN CONTROLS panel for focusing.
Set the pixel number to 512 × 512 pixels with a pixel dwell time of 4.8 µs on the CONFIGURATION panel.
Set the lock-in amplifier input range (typically 5 mV) to be twice the maximal signal voltage.
Set the low-pass filter to match the pixel dwell time (4.8 µs).
Set the imaging resolution to 2,048 × 2,048 pixels for a 175 µm² field of view.
Check the SAVE function on the MAIN CONTROLS panel and ensure the SRS channel is selected on the CHANNELS panel.
Set the interval time between two frames to be 180 s (3 min) on the MAIN CONTROLS channel.
Set the acquisition number to 480 for time-lapse imaging over 24 hours.
Start automated imaging acquisition using the LOOP function on the MAIN CONTROLS panel.
Check for focal drift due to temperature instability during the first hour of imaging.
Process collected images using ImageJ.
Measure the LD/cell body area ratio for LD quantification.
Measure the mean SRS intensity of total LDs for LD quantification.
Threshold and zero non-cellular pixels in SRS images at 2,854 cm-1 to measure cell body area.
Threshold and zero non-LD pixels in SRS images to measure LD area and intensity.
